comparisons.peer_topic: Shareholder Returns and Stock Repurchase Program
comparisons.peer_summary: AMD returned $862 million to shareholders in 2024 through stock repurchases, with $4.7 billion remaining available under a program that has no termination date and may be suspended or discontinued at any time.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and AMD disclose active stock repurchase programs with no expiration dates and explicitly state that the programs do not obligate the company to acquire any stock. However, they differ significantly in the scale of authorization and activity: MU has authorized $10 billion with $7.19 billion repurchased as of August 2024, whereas AMD returned $862 million in 2024 with $4.7 billion remaining available as of December 2024, indicating AMD had repurchased less of its available authorization relative to its total program size in the fiscal year compared to MU's high utilization rate.

sentences.text: Our Board of Directors has authorized the discretionary repurchase of up to $10 billion of our outstanding common stock through open-market purchases, block trades, privately-negotiated transactions, derivative transactions, and/or pursuant to Rule 10b5-1 trading plans.

The repurchase authorization has no expiration date, does not obligate us to acquire any common stock, and is subject to market conditions and our ongoing determination of the best use of available cash.
Through August 29, 2024, we had repurchased an aggregate of $7.19 billion of the authorized amount.
During the twelve months ended December 28, 2024, we returned a total of $862 million to shareholders through the repurchase of 5.9 million shares of common stock under our stock repurchase program.
As of December 28, 2024, $4.7 billion remained available for future stock repurchases under this program.
The stock repurchase program does not obligate us to acquire any common stock, has no termination date and may be suspended or discontinued at any time.

comparisons.peer_topic: Stock Repurchase Program Utilization and Fiscal Year Activity
comparisons.peer_summary: Broadcom utilized all $20 billion of authorized stock repurchase amounts prior to expiration on December 31, 2023, having repurchased approximately 67 million shares for $7,176 million in fiscal year 2024 and 91 million shares for $5,824 million in fiscal year 2023.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies report substantial stock repurchase activity, but differ in program structure and timeline. MU reports an ongoing, open-ended $10 billion authorization with $7.19 billion utilized by August 2024. In contrast, AVGO reports that it had fully utilized two prior programs totaling $20 billion by the expiration date of December 31, 2023, having repurchased $7,176 million in fiscal 2024. While both highlight large repurchase volumes, MU's program is currently active with remaining capacity, whereas AVGO's disclosed programs had expired after full utilization.

sentences.text: Our Board of Directors has authorized the discretionary repurchase of up to $10 billion of our outstanding common stock through open-market purchases, block trades, privately-negotiated transactions, derivative transactions, and/or pursuant to Rule 10b5-1 trading plans.

In December 2021, our Board of Directors authorized a stock repurchase program to repurchase up to $10 billion of our common stock from time to time through December 31, 2022, which was subsequently extended to December 31, 2023.

All $20 billion of the authorized amount under these stock repurchase programs was utilized prior to expiration on December 31, 2023.
